outcome: Redington turns operations scripts into reviewed, version-controlled automation that runs the same way every time and leaves an audit trail.
overview: Telecom operations teams carry a large amount of repeated configuration work — provisioning, compliance remediation, change execution across thousands of network and server elements — and most of it is done by hand under a change window. Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform turns that work into reviewed, version-controlled content that runs the same way every time and leaves a record of what it did. The point is not that scripts appear; scripts already exist. It is that they become shared, auditable and safe to hand to someone who did not write them. Redington measures change execution time and change-failure rate against the pre-automation baseline.

benefits.text: Repeated changes execute identically, and each run leaves an auditable record
benefits.limits: Only for work that has been converted into reviewed content; anything still done by hand is unaffected and usually stays that way longest

benefits.text: Automation content becomes a shared asset rather than personal scripts on a jump host
benefits.limits: Requires someone to own content review; without it the platform accumulates the same unreviewed scripts in a nicer place

benefits.text: Change windows carry more work because execution is no longer the constraint
benefits.limits: The approval process, not the execution, is often the real constraint; measure both before attributing the gain

residency: Control node, content repository and execution environments all run inside the customer estate; device credentials stay in the customer’s own vault

notFor.situation: A team already standardised on another automation platform with reviewed content
notFor.why: The value is in the content and the review process, and neither transfers by changing the runner

notFor.situation: An estate whose devices have no programmatic interface
notFor.why: Automation reaches devices through their APIs or CLIs; equipment with neither cannot be brought in

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Red Hat implementation partner · Duration: 6–10 weeks to a first automated change class in production
Support model: Vendor subscription support for the platform; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional content retainer with an agreed monthly backlog.
1) Assessment — change-class inventory, execution-time baseline and candidate selection
2) Design — role model, credential brokering, inventory sources and the content review path
3) Build — controller and execution nodes, hub, Git integration and the first content set
4) Operate and hand over — first change class running under change control, reviewers trained
deliverables: A change executes from reviewed content with no operator holding the target credential
Every execution produces a run record identifying content version, operator and result
A customer engineer takes an unfamiliar change class from draft to merged content unaided
effort: 6–10 weeks to a first automated change class in production
